headline: Granted variances for 6 Pearl Street garage, 19 Aiken Street sunroom, and 67 Frost Road garage; denied 32 Crystal Ave group recovery residence.
summary: The board granted three zoning variance requests for projects at 6 Pearl Street, 19 Aiken Street, and 67 Frost Road. It denied a request to operate a 10-bed men's group recovery residence at 32 Crystal Ave. It tabled a request for a child group daycare at 1.5 Hood Rd to 9/17/26.
decisions: Granted a variance for a commercial garage at 6 Pearl Street, 5-0.
Granted a variance for a sunroom at 19 Aiken Street, 5-0.
Granted a variance for a two-car garage with an ADU at 67 Frost Road, 5-0.
Denied a variance for a 10-bed men's group recovery residence at 32 Crystal Ave, 0-5.
Tabled the request for a child group daycare at 1.5 Hood Rd to 9/17/26.

# TOWN OF DERRY

## Zoning Board of Adjustment

## MEETING MINUTES – September 3, 2026

**MEMBERS PRESENT**

- Lynn Perkins, Chair
- Crystal Morin
- Richard Tripp
- James Dietzel

**MEMBERS ABSENT**

- Craig Corbett, Vice Chair

**ALTERNATES PRESENT**

- Michael Donlon

- Jason Dragani

Keri Owen, Code Enforcement

Minutes prepared by: Tina Guilford, Town Clerk

## I. CALL TO ORDER:

Mr. Perkins called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the salute to the flag. Instructions were given on safety. Also noted the meeting is audio and video recorded.

## II. PUBLIC HEARING

**26-118 (Tabled from August 20, 2026, Meeting)**

**Applicant:** Cocuzzo Enterprises, LLC

**Owner:** 6 Pearl Street, LLC

Parcel ID 30092

6 Pearl Street

Zoned: CBD

The applicant is requesting a variance to the terms of Article VI, Section 165-33B of the Town of Derry Zoning Ordinance to permit the use of the existing rear of the property as a contractor yard and allow the construction of a contractor garage for use from the abutting property at 27 Franklin St.

Mr. Perkins asked Mr. Obimba to sit in on case 26-118 filling in for Mr. Dragani.

Mr. Perkins asked if the applicants had anything they had to start with.

Applicants responded that they don't really have anything significant to say since the last meeting. I understand that the board was reaching out to town council and safety services about some questions, and I know— my understanding is those questions have been answered, and we're hoping to move forward. Mr. Perkins responded essentially, what we're looking for now, you've kind of amended your position, which was that you wanted to put a garage on 6 Pearl and access it from Franklin Street, correct?

Applicant responded that is correct.

Mr. Perkins - This is Franklin Street parcel. You are going to be moving your materials, or have moved them, off of Pearl Street onto Franklin Street, isolating the contractor use idea. Is that correct?

Applicant - That's the idea, yes.

Mr. Perkins asked Ms. Owen how the Town feels in regards to your liability and your concerns addressing access from Franklin onto Pearl, and anything else that comes under your purview?

Ms. Owens stated that based on discussions with legal counsel, and we also conferred with the fire department on addressing and access and safety regulations. So, what we are basically going through all our due diligence, there doesn't appear to be any immediate concerns from a town perspective. The owner may wish to choose to explore the need for easements if they decide to, but the town would not get involved in a civil matter. That would be private and any such agreements would be on the owner's behalf and would be so if the properties were to sell. Site access and addressing would be reviewed and determined by the fire department during the TRC process, which would be part of the planning board application.

Mr. Perkins asked if the board were to approve this, subject to town permits and inspections, the applicant would be required to review with TRC. Am I correct?

Ms. Owens confirmed they would be required to complete the site plan process with the planning board, which includes the TRC process.

Mr. Perkins opens up to questions from the board.

Mr. Obimba – I am all set.

Mr. Deitzel - is it my understanding that if you were to put this garage on the Franklin Street property where that lawn is, that it would conform, but you simply feel that you don't want to wreck the lawn and for aesthetic purposes, would it conform if you were to put it on that lawn?

Applicant – I believe that it would.

Mr. Tripp - so the only variance that you're asking for is to be able to construct a contractor garage on Pearl. And that would be the only use you would be making of the Pearl Street address.

Applicant – The reason we need a variance is because the district, Central Business District, allows for combined residential and, like, multifamily and commercial use, but it's supposed to be an over/under situation, which does not exist. Right now, there's a three-unit building, residential building on the property. And according to town records, it is not grandfathered commercial use. That was that use was started in error, and that's the situation we are looking to get a remedy for, that the town has asked us to come in for site plan determination, and this got flagged, so we're trying to get it properly permitted. And so, we're supposed to have, like, an over/under situation. You can't have that. So, it's technically a use variance to allow contractor use on the same lot as residential use without that situation, the over/under thing.

Mr. Tripp - But that would not include the storage of construction material on Pearl Street?

Applicant - This is correct.

Ms. Owen - If I may clarify, this property is located in the Central Business District. Mixed use is permitted, with residential. Residential is not permitted below the second floor. So that kind of comes into play, adding commercial use onto the property. It's creating the mixed-use condition. They have residential existing on the property. This mixed use doesn't really align with the ordinance as far as the configuration with residential above. That's the request for variance.

Ms. Morin – My question has been asked and answered.

Mr. Perkins - we're to be clear now, the original motion, Ms. Owen, you just keep your ear to this, is that the request in the application is to permit the use of the existing rear of the property as a contractor yard and allow the construction of a contractor garage for use from the abutting property at 27 Franklin Street. We are eliminating, I believe now, this as referenced and directed towards the Pearl Street, the contractor yard version, correct?

Ms. Owen – Correct

Mr. Perkins - I believe that we are eliminating in this a contractor yard use.

Ms. Owens - Correct.

Mr. Perkins - Which you are shifting onto the Franklin Street parcel, correct?

Applicant - Yes.

Mr. Perkins - you are still looking for what you call the contractor garage, but I don't care if it's called a contractor garage or just a garage myself. Are we having a conflict there, Ms. Owen? Are we to stipulate that the garage is specifically a contractor garage, or is it just being called a garage?

Ms. Owen - It's called a garage, but it's being used for the commercial business operation from the adjacent lot.

Mr. Perkins - And when we when we speak of it being used for the contractor from the abutting lot, are we just stipulating that it is a garage for somebody's lettered truck? Is that what we're looking at, or are we defining contractor garage differently?

Ms. Owens - can you clarify your question, please?

Mr. Perkins - I think that what we discussed in one of the past meetings on this case was that somebody could build a garage and rent out the spaces, correct? And now the owner under the trust, the LLC owns both properties under different LLC names, but it still doesn't restrict the owner from Pearl Street to rent a garage space to whoever with having a truck, right, a lettered vehicle. And I think that's calling it a contractor garage, so to speak, where there's no specified materials there, again, this is going to have to go through TRC and planning, correct?

Ms. Owen - Correct.

Mr. Perkins - I did hear some verbiage to Mr. Tripp's question that may indicate some latitude that may be looked for. To that point, somebody could have two by fours in their pickup and park in the garage, and no one knows about it, correct? So, what's the stipulation of the materials that are there, and if they're in a truck and they're in that garage, does it matter, right? That becomes the gray area. What I'm trying to do is give you what I'm looking for for the contractor garage stipulation. To me, as I think I've already indicated in a past meeting, that this could be just a garage, and that's what we're giving the usage for, but we're not giving usage as a contractor yard at Pearl Street. That is all our understanding, correct? And that works for Code Enforcement as well. What I'm really trying to articulate here is how this motion is to be constructed as it's weaned its way away from what the original request was. And I just want to make sure that all parties are clear on this. If you decide at some later point that you're going to start putting materials outside on Pearl Street, it doesn't remove your contractor garage, but you end up back here before us again, correct?

Applicant – Yes, sir.

Mr. Perkins – Are we on the same page, Ms. Owen?

Ms. Owens - We are on the same page, but I would like to clarify that 27 Franklin Street is not permitted to have a contractor yard either. They could be permitted to have small amounts of accessory storage space in the yard, but how it exists today would be considered a contractor yard.

Mr. Perkins - And so if there's any conflicts on Franklin Street that, again, could bring up a red flag, and you could have concerns there as well. This board, for this matter, right now, is only looking at the fact that you wanted a garage. How you deal with your storage, what you park there, we are not giving you any permission to do that. That's outside of our purview. Is that fair enough?

Applicant - That's fair enough. I believe and correct me if I'm wrong, but I think the variance is for the use of the property as part of the contractor's business and not explicitly for the garage, which would be as you said, he would be allowed to just build a garage. It's the use of the property that's at stake.

Mr. Perkins - That is correct. And that use is as a contractor yard on Pearl Street. And, you know, again, this approval for, I guess, a garage does not give you a green light for anything else beyond that. And for that matter, this board, I guess, is going to clear this case. And you had an opportunity perhaps to consider a lot line adjustment that would make part of Pearl Street part of Franklin Street, correct? And you chose not to go that way as well.

Applicant – Correct.

Mr. Perkins - The board has heard the narrative on this. I guess in some ways we have to amend this motion a little bit. Does anybody have any questions or concerns?

Mr. Tripp – I believe Ms. Owens said a contractor yard is not permitted on Franklin Street either?

Ms. Owens – Correct. They would be permitted to have exterior storage, but not what we would consider a contractor yard.

Mr. Perkins – This is a garage, what relief are they looking for?

Ms. Owen - Section 165-33(b)(5), and I'm going to go to subsection (b)(III)(I). All residential so this is multi-unit residential uses are permitted as mixed use in conjunction with permitted non-residential uses subject to the following limitations. All residential units permitted under the subsection shall be prohibited below the second floor. So, the residential is in the primary existing structure on the property. There'll be a detached garage containing commercial use, and I think that that's the relief that's needed. I believe that the variance would be required for in this condition. It was contractor use is permitted in CBD, and a contractor yard is not. They've removed the contractor yard. We can call it a garage, but now you're creating the mixed use on the property with commercial and residential. And so, I think that that is the relief, the variance that's needed.

Mr. Perkins – so at this point it is not a contractor garage but a commercial garage, for use from the abutting property at 27 Franklin.

Applicant – Correct.

## MOTION TO ENTER DELIBRATION

Mr. Tripp made a motion to enter deliberation.

Seconded by Mr. Obimba. All in favor, none opposed.

Mr. Dietzel - I think since we simplified it quite a bit then I'm just going to go by the five criteria. The reason I asked my question about whether he could build a conforming garage on the on the Franklin Street property is because primarily due to the fifth criterion, the hardship criterion. It says, "For purposes of this paragraph, the little no fair and substantial relationship exists between the general public purposes and the ordinance provision." And it's almost like by conforming with the ordinance strictly, we'd wind up with a less desirable result than granting the variance because that piece of property with its lawn is attractive aesthetically, and also can be used in the future if they decide that the lawn is not the best use. I think I'd almost rather have a non-conforming structure than a conforming one. And so having said that, reviewing the other five criteria I think it is in the best interest of the town to first of all, clean it up, which is the ultimate goal. It'll allow them to continue the business. I don't think property values will be diminished at all. And I think, after all is reviewed and all the all the TRC and planning and everything, I think that it'll be okay. I think it meets the five criteria.

Mr. Obimba - I echo the similar sentiments as Mr. Dietzel. I like how we've cleaned up the motion. It makes it very simple for code enforcement to work with the applicants. And it's very clear. I think I've been on this case for on the sidelines for a while. It's, it's clear on the on the variance they're seeking. I don't see any problem with the five criteria just because it's already has some non-conforming, usages on the property. The spirit of the ordinance here is to promote health, public safety, and general welfare to the community. We are already using that as a business. I don't see how that gets greatly affected by granting this variance. I think the motion is clear enough.

Mr. Tripp – I am all set.

Ms. Morin – My only concern was the public interest and that has been addressed.

Mr. Perkins – Without being repetitive, it would be absurd for me to disagree at this point.

## MOTION TO LEAVE DELIBRATION

Mr. Tripp made a motion to leave deliberation.

Seconded by Mr. Deitzel, All in favor, none opposed.

**26-125**

**Applicant:** Dolores Desiderio

**Owner:** Dolores Desiderio

Parcel ID 26030-001

19 Aiken Street

Zoned: MHDR

The applicant is requesting a variance to the terms of Article VI, Section 165-45.1.B.d of the Town of Derry Zoning Ordinance to allow the construction of a sunroom 11.5 feet from the side property line at its closest point when 15 feet is required.

Mr. Perkins asked Mr. Henry to sit in on case 26-125.

Mr. Timothy Lynch spoke for the applicant and read the application and the 5 criteria.

The first point is that the variance is not contrary to public interest. And our response to that is the requested variance of 11.5 feet for side yard setback to accommodate a corner of the proposed sunroom would only impact a 15-square-foot area within the standard 15-foot setback. This would increase the property value without adversely impacting the abutters or the neighborhood. And just to point out, that 15-square-foot area is equal to a half a sheet of plywood. The second point, the spirit of the ordinance is observed because the variance would not adversely impact the abutters, negatively affect the surrounding property values, or change the character of the neighborhood. Substantial justice is done because the lot is a very restrictive odd shape, almost pie-shaped, requiring a small variance to accommodate a corner of the proposed sunroom. Item four, the values of surrounding properties are not diminished because the variance and construction of the sunroom would increase the property value, benefiting the value of surrounding properties. There are no negative impacts to the surrounding properties. Item five, literal enforcement of the provision of the ordinance would result in an unnecessary hardship. The odd shape of the lot is restrictive, and a small variance is necessary to accommodate one corner of the sunroom to provide reasonable use while meeting the general intent of the ordinance. The existing house is small. It's, it's 1,310 square feet and has one common room. The addition of a sunroom is a a is a significant improvement for the period that the owner has to spend at home while undergoing treatment for a medical condition. And those are the five points.

I think that the biggest point is it's a very restrictive property. As I said, there's one common room. She uses a deck when the weather is good to get a little more room. She's spending a great deal of time at the residence because she is undergoing medical treatment. And as I said, we're talking about encroaching on that 15-foot setback by half a sheet of plywood. So, we're not talking much. It's just at the corner of the sunroom.

Mr. Perkins - You're replacing a deck that's there now?

Applicant - Correct. We're tying the sunroom into the existing building. The roof ties in, the walls tie in. So, you're also limited on where you can tie in to the building.

Mr. Perkins - for the record, the board has 2 letters of recommendation from abutters that will be read into the record later.

Ms. Owens - I'll just start by reiterating what the applicant has stated. They're requesting a variance to allow the construction of a 14-foot by 14-foot sunroom 11 and a half feet off of the side property line at its closest point when 15 feet is required. The property is located in the medium-high-density residential zoning district, which requires a minimum of a 15-foot side setback. Therefore, the variance is required. The applicant proposes to replace the existing deck, as we can see, was 11-foot by 12-foot, and now build an enclosed sunroom measuring 14-foot by 14. The existing single-family residence was constructed in 2015. The existing parcel is approximately just under a quarter of an acre, and is serviced by municipal water and sewer. The existing single-family residence is considered conforming with respect to the front setback requirements pursuant to Article 3, Section 165-10, which allows the required setback to be determined by averaging the setbacks of principal structures located within 300 feet of the property on the same side of the street. So, we're using that, which was what permitted the existing single-family home. We are confirming with that section and that was permitted at that time that the front setback is preexisting nonconforming or is conforming per this Article 165-10. The proposed sunroom addition would expand the existing footprint while maintaining the established residential use of the property. The variance pertains solely to the side setback, and if approved, appropriate permits and inspections are required.

## 26-126

Applicant: Patricia M. Panciocco, Esquire - Paciocco Law, LLC

Owner: Robert Scott Rowe

Parcel ID 02149-014

67 Frost Rd

Zoned: LMDR

The applicant is requesting a variance to the terms of Article III, Section 165-25.a and Article VI, Section 165-47.B.4 of the Town of Derry Zoning Ordinance to allow the construction of a 2-car attached garage with ADU above 25.1 feet from the front property line where 15 feet is required due to the right-of-way.

Mr. Perkins asked Mr. Donlan to sit in on case 26-126.

Ms. Panciocco reads the application, including the 5 criteria into the record.

First criteria, the variance will not be contrary to the public interest. For the variance to be contrary to the public interest, it must markedly alter the essential character of the neighborhood or threaten the public health, safety, or welfare of the community. Harrington v. Warner. The subject property is located in the low-medium-density residential district in an area of Derry where there are primarily single-family homes located on one and two-acre lots. The owner is proposing to add a two-car attached garage to his existing single-family home and finish approximately 911 square feet above the garage as an ADU as he will reside with his daughter, Danielle. The plans for the structure have been submitted with the application as Exhibit F. Due to a 50-foot right-of-way, which was laid out by a 1980 subdivision, a 35-foot front setback applies to the northerly sideline of the applicant's lot. That is shown on Exhibit B. There is also a 20-foot-wide drainage easement extending along the lot's northerly boundary. The exterior renderings for the ADU attached as Exhibit F show the front elevation was designed to match the existing home when viewed from Frost Road. For this reason, the ADU will not be seen from the road and will not change the character of the or the of the area or threaten the public health, safety, or welfare, as shown in the two photos attached as Exhibit D of structures that are in the area. For the spirit of the ordinance to be observed, it must markedly conflict with its intended purpose. The owner is requesting a variance from the 35-foot front setback applied to the northerly sideline of his lot due to the unimproved roadway right-of-way created in 1980. The purpose of setbacks is to ensure adequate spacing between structures and between structures and roads. Greater setbacks generally apply to roads where traffic is anticipated to exist. The right-of-way, however, has existed on plans for 46 years and has yet to be improved. It is very unlikely there will never be a roadway built in the right-of-way due to the stream that flows across the right-of-way shown on Exhibit E1, where there is also a wetland, and its topography drops off and then goes up dramatically, actually about 20 feet, as shown on Exhibit E2. There is also a wetland located on the parcel directly abutting the rear of the lot, and collectively, these physical challenges likely explain why the right-of-way has not been improved. It would not be contrary to the spirit and intent of the ordinance to grant the owner's request for a modest reduction of the front setback requirement being applied to his side lot line to accommodate the construction of the garage and the ADU. Substantial justice will be done by granting the variance because, for it to be done, the benefit to the owner must outweigh any public harm. Since it is very unlikely the right-of-way will ever be improved due to its physical challenges, there will be no loss to the public by granting this modest relief to allow the garage and ADU to be constructed on the lot. The values of the surrounding properties will not be diminished. The owner's construction plans attached as Exhibit F show the exterior elevation of the proposed ADU is designed to match the exterior of his existing home. The house located directly across Frost Road from the lot is similarly styled. That's shown on Exhibit C. There is also a much larger duplex located on Frost Road with an ADU near the lot that's also, uh, similarly styled. Collectively, these photos confirm the owner's proposed improvement will blend in with the area and not diminish surrounding property values. Literal enforcement of the provisions of the ordinance would result in an unnecessary hardship. The purpose of the of the unnecessary hardship, it means owing to the special conditions of the property that distinguish it from other properties in this area. The special conditions of this lot include there being no area available along the southerly side of the home to add the proposed structure, which is the opposite end of where the garage addition is proposed. In addition, there is the right-of-way. There's a 20-foot-wide drainage easement extending the full length of the northerly sideline inside the limits of the lot. That is shown on Exhibit A. There is also a stream that crosses through the right-of-way to the lot directly on the opposite side of the right-of-way that empties into a pond further down Frost Road. The photos shown on Exhibit D also show a very large outcropping alleged located directly behind the existing home where the well and a patio are also located before the topography drops down dramatically. These existing improvements and conditions prevent the garage ADU from being placed elsewhere, um, behind the home. No fair and substantial relationship exists between the general public purpose of the ordinance, which is the setback ordinance, and the specific application to that provision to this property. The proposed garage ADU cannot be moved back further due to the pool patio and ledge outcropping, and the proposed ADU cannot be placed on the other side of the building because the existing home is too close to the southerly boundary. The purpose of a front setback is to ensure there is adequate space between the structures and vehicles traveling along a public way. As applied to the northerly sideline of the lot, the right-of-way planted 46 years ago has never been improved, and upon closer examination of its physical characteristics and consideration of the permitting that would be required to improve the right-of-way, it is highly unlikely it ever will be. In addition, the relief being requested here is approximately 10 feet it's actually 9 feet 11 inches in the front and 7 feet in the rear. It's actually 6 and a half feet. Exceeding the distance required by the side setback otherwise required in the MLMTR zone if the side setback requirement were applied to this particular lot. But because it's a Connor lot, the front setback applies on both sides. The proposed use is reasonable. The relief is 7 feet and 10 feet for the front and rear setbacks of the garage and the ADU, and it's reasonable in light of the age of the right-of-way and the likelihood it will remain unimproved.

When we first looked at this and, and I spoke with Ms. Owens about this she wondered if we needed the variance because the plan originally from 1980 showed a 15-foot side setback. Along the right-of-way. But given the extent of the investment my client is making into this particular improvement, to be cautious, we elected to come before the board and ask for relief from a front setback to ensure that there was no violation in the future. The property is really substantially encumbered. As you can see from the site plan, you've got the drainage easement that goes across the lot and then down the side that goes out under Frost Road. But there's also another drainage easement that you can see on the old recorded plans that actually crosses the lot and continues, to the east where it crosses the other lots on that side of Frost Road and empties into a detention basin. There really is not a lot of area or wiggle room for Mr. Rowe to work within to accomplish this desire. He is moving into the ADU himself with his daughter who is disabled. They're both here tonight with me and his other daughter and their family are moving into his home in the main house. So, this is really his only option to be able to remain in place on the site and have a separate living space. The topography drop also, if you look on Exhibit E, it's E1 or E2, is really substantial when you go in. There are photographs of the right-of-way from the road. As you go in towards where the stream crosses the right-of-way, there's like a 20-foot drop in that area. So, the chances of that ever being improved are pretty slim. The topography is shown on E2. So, the relief is also fairly modest and well within what it would have been if we had elected to just follow the side setback.

Mr. Perkins - what was your argument or point as to why the new construction cannot slide back so it's flush with the front of the other of the main home?

Applicant - I'm sorry. I didn't understand your question, Mr. Chairman.

Mr. Perkins - Did you did you specify why the ADU can't be constructed so that it was flush with the front of the existing house?

Applicant - If we were to slide the structure further back, Mr. Chairman, we would still need relief from the ordinance. And directly behind where the ADU is proposed, there's also a patio which is in the well radius, we're moving closer to the well. And there is a photograph also included as an exhibit that shows a very, very large outcropping of ledge.

Ms. Owen - As the applicant stated, requesting a variance to allow the construction of a two-car attached garage with an ADU above to 25.1 feet from the side property line where 35 feet could be required due to the existing right-of-way.
